explanation: 1) The DC gain is \(G(0)\). 2) Substitute \(s=0\): \(G(0)=\dfrac{12(5)}{(3)(4)}=\dfrac{60}{12}\). 3) So the DC gain is \(5\).

front: Find the transfer function \(T(s)=Y(s)/U(s)\) and its poles for the system \(\ddot{y}+7\dot{y}+12y=3u(t)\) with zero initial conditions.
explanation: 1) Laplace transform with zero initial conditions: \((s^{2}+7s+12)Y(s)=3U(s)\). 2) Divide: \(T(s)=\dfrac{3}{s^{2}+7s+12}\). 3) Factor the denominator: \(s^{2}+7s+12=(s+3)(s+4)\), so the poles are \(s=-3\) and \(s=-4\).

front: A second-order system has characteristic equation \(s^{2}+4s+25=0\). Find the natural frequency \(\omega_n\), the damping ratio \(\zeta\), and classify the response.
explanation: 1) Compare with \(s^{2}+2\zeta\omega_n s+\omega_n^{2}\). 2) \(\omega_n^{2}=25\Rightarrow\omega_n=5\ \text{rad/s}\). 3) \(2\zeta\omega_n=4\Rightarrow\zeta=\dfrac{4}{2(5)}=0.4\). 4) Since \(0<\zeta<1\), the response is underdamped.

front: A second-order system has damping ratio \(\zeta=0.6\). Estimate the percent overshoot of its unit-step response.
Classify the transient response and stability of a system with characteristic equation \(s^{2}+7s+10=0\).
back: Overdamped and stable (real, distinct poles \(s=-2\) and \(s=-5\)).
explanation: 1) Factor: \(s^{2}+7s+10=(s+2)(s+5)\). 2) Poles are \(s=-2\) and \(s=-5\). 3) Both are real, distinct, and negative, so the system is stable and the response is overdamped.

front: Use the Routh-Hurwitz criterion to determine the number of right-half-plane roots of \(s^{4}+2s^{3}+3s^{2}+4s+5=0\).
back: Two right-half-plane roots; the system is unstable.

front: A unity-feedback system has open-loop transfer function \(G(s)=\dfrac{K}{s(s+2)(s+6)}\). Find the range of \(K>0\) for closed-loop stability.
For a unity-feedback system with \(G(s)=\dfrac{40}{(s+2)(s+4)}\), find the steady-state error to a unit-step input.
explanation: 1) This is a type-0 system; use the position error constant \(K_p=\lim_{s\to0}G(s)=\dfrac{40}{(2)(4)}=5\). 2) For a unit step, \(e_{ss}=\dfrac{1}{1+K_p}\). 3) \(e_{ss}=\dfrac{1}{1+5}=\dfrac{1}{6}\approx0.167\).

front: For a unity-feedback system with \(G(s)=\dfrac{80}{s(s+4)}\), find the steady-state error to a unit-ramp input.
explanation: 1) This is a type-1 system; use the velocity error constant \(K_v=\lim_{s\to0}sG(s)=\dfrac{80}{4}=20\). 2) For a unit ramp, \(e_{ss}=\dfrac{1}{K_v}\). 3) \(e_{ss}=\dfrac{1}{20}=0.05\).

front: A unity-feedback type-0 system has \(G(s)=\dfrac{30}{(s+3)(s+5)}\). Find the steady-state error to a unit-ramp input.
explanation: 1) The velocity error constant is \(K_v=\lim_{s\to0}sG(s)\). 2) With no pole at the origin, \(K_v=0\cdot\dfrac{30}{(3)(5)}=0\). 3) For a ramp, \(e_{ss}=\dfrac{1}{K_v}=\infty\); a type-0 system cannot follow a ramp input.

front: A first-order system has transfer function \(G(s)=\dfrac{8}{s+4}\). Find its time constant \(\tau\) and its 2% settling time.
explanation: 1) The pole is at \(s=-4\), so \(\tau=\dfrac{1}{4}=0.25\ \text{s}\). 2) For a first-order system the 2% settling time is \(T_s\approx4\tau\). 3) \(T_s\approx4(0.25)=1\ \text{s}\).

front: For the second-order system \(T(s)=\dfrac{25}{s^{2}+2s+25}\), estimate the 2% settling time and the damped natural frequency.
A system has forward-path transfer function \(G(s)=\dfrac{20}{s+3}\) and a negative-feedback path \(H(s)=0.25\). Find the closed-loop transfer function.
A unity-feedback system has forward-path transfer function \(G(s)=\dfrac{2}{s(s+3)}\). Find the closed-loop transfer function and its poles.
explanation: 1) For unity feedback, \(T(s)=\dfrac{G}{1+G}=\dfrac{2}{s(s+3)+2}\). 2) Expand: \(s(s+3)+2=s^{2}+3s+2\). 3) Factor \((s+1)(s+2)\), so the closed-loop poles are \(s=-1\) and \(s=-2\).

front: For \(G(s)=\dfrac{20}{s+5}\), state the break (corner) frequency of its Bode plot and the DC gain in decibels.
explanation: 1) The pole at \(s=-5\) sets the corner frequency \(\omega=5\ \text{rad/s}\). 2) The DC gain is \(G(0)=\dfrac{20}{5}=4\). 3) In decibels, \(20\log_{10}(4)\approx12\ \text{dB}\).
